title: This Fish Hits Bugs Above the Water Through a Surface That Lies
subject: archerfish

scenes.text: This fish shoots insects off branches, and it aims through a surface that lies to it.
Water bends light, so the bug isn't where the fish sees it. The true angle can be off by up to twenty-five degrees.
The archerfish corrects for that, then spits a jet of water to knock the insect down.
And it shapes the jet. The back of the stream moves faster than the front.
The stream breaks into blobs, and the fast ones catch up and merge into one big blob that hits harder.
A bigger punch than its mouth could deliver alone, from a fish that aims through a distorted view.

description:
This fish shoots insects off branches while aiming through a surface that bends light.
Scientists found it corrects for refraction and shapes its water jet so the blobs merge into one stronger hit.
Could you hit a target like that?
first_comment: Would you rather have an archerfish's aim or a pistol shrimp's snap?
